## Risks and Mitigations says "An attendee leaks into the DTO through a later edit | L | H | Task 7's VALIDATE greps for it and exits non-zero; the DTO's type has no field to hold one"; Task 7's actual VALIDATE is `grep -rn --include=*.ts -E "\.(attendees|reminders|recurrence)\b" src/ | grep -vE "hasGuests|^\s*(//|\*)"` — the exclusion filter matches on the bare substring "hasGuests" appearing ANYWHERE on the offending line, not on the line being the sanctioned derivation shape. A genuine leak such as `const leaked = raw.attendees; // still just hasGuests-adjacent` or any stray comment/identifier containing that substring on the same line as a raw `.attendees`/`.reminders`/`.recurrence` access is silently excluded and the gate reports PASS. An Implementer relying on this VALIDATE as the leak tripwire the Risks table promises could ship a real PII leak that this gate was specifically authored to catch.

Task 4's ACTION says "Run npm run db:generate, then READ the emitted SQL before applying and confirm it is purely additive" (about THIS task's own migration); its VALIDATE instead inspects `fs.readdirSync('migrations').filter(n=>n.endsWith('.sql')).sort().pop()` — the lexicographically newest .sql file by sort order, not necessarily the file this task generated. Relies on an unstated zero-padded sequential-numbering assumption rather than proving the claim directly.
